question: When comparing crude death rates between India and Japan, the difference observed directly reflects the true difference in disease burden between the two countries.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Crude death rates are influenced by the age composition of the population. Japan's older demographic pushes its crude rate higher independent of actual health quality. Age-standardisation removes this compositional effect before comparing.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Crude rates are confounded by the age structure of each population. Japan has a far older population, so its crude death rate is inflated by age alone, not by worse health. Age-standardised rates must be used for valid comparison.
